rgb: A compact room is shown with a stone-tiled floor, an inset wall shelf on the left holding framed pictures and brass lamps, a small illuminated bowl on the floor before the shelf, and an open doorway on the right. Two shirtless men in dark lower garments and necklaces stand next to one another—under 0.5 metres apart—against the back wall to the shelf’s right, initially around 1.5 to 2 metres ahead of the camera wearer; their torsos face the camera, but their heads stay cropped beyond the upper frame edge throughout, so their gaze cannot be seen. Moving left to right through the five frames, the wearer advances steadily and angles the camera downward at the men, reducing the distance from about 1.8 metres in frame one to 1.2 metres in frame two, 0.7 metres in frame three, and below 0.5 metres in frames four and five, as the shelf and floor bowl disappear past the left edge. Nothing lies within the wearer’s arm’s reach during the first two frames, but both men are reachable by frame three. In frame four, the man on the left lifts his left hand near the lens, while an extended right arm with an orange wristband comes from the lower left and touches the right man’s right arm; another person’s hands and white garment are partly visible along the lower-right edge. By frame five, the downward-facing camera captures only the two men’s lower torsos and legs from within 0.4 metres: the right man clasps his hands before his waist, the left man is partly hidden by the left border, the wearer’s own foot appears at bottom center, and a bare right arm extends upward from the lower right to touch the left man’s waist.
depth: The depth rendering depicts a compact enclosed room, including a recessed shelf along the left wall (~1.5–2.5 m distant in frame 1), the stone floor beneath it, and two bare-chested men beside each other (~0.2–0.4 m apart) ahead of the camera wearer, with their heads cut off above the frame. Over the five frames, the wearer moves closer while tilting downward, progressing from ~1.5–2.0 m away in frame 1 to ~0.3–0.6 m away—comfortably inside arm’s reach—during frames 3–5. Meanwhile, both men lean forward and bring their arms down toward a lit floor lamp at the lower left and toward the wearer’s lower body; in frame 5, the wearer’s right arm extends from the bottom right and touches the left man’s waist at ~0.3 m. Their gazes cannot be determined because their heads remain outside the upper edge, although their torso surfaces are oriented toward the wearer and somewhat leftward. Relative to the RGB strip, in which severe shadows and dark garments conceal spatial edges, the depth gradients distinctly separate frame 4’s foreground raised palm and crossing arms from the torsos behind, while also recording the continuous distance change across the floor and shelf. The depth output is nevertheless unreliable once the men become extremely close in frames 3–5: the background floor falls to solid black, and relative depth saturates into uniform white over the nearest shoulders and chests.
segmentation: In frames 1 and 2, the segmentation output separates the two men standing before the camera wearer: the left man is colored pink and closes from ~1.5–2.0 m to ~1.0–1.5 m, while the slightly nearer right man is colored brown and closes from ~1.2–1.8 m to ~0.8–1.2 m, positioned ~0.3 m to the right. Both generally face the wearer, with their heads cropped beyond the upper edge. As they move to arm’s-reach distance (~0.3–0.6 m) through frames 3–5, the men bend downward and their arms overlap across the foreground; in frame 5, the wearer’s own right forearm appears from the lower right and contacts the left man’s garment. The map clearly traces the division between their neighboring bodies in frames 1–2 and, in frame 5, extracts the wearer’s reaching arm as a separate pink mask against the dark wrap, which merges with dark shadow in RGB. It does not, however, segment the wall shelf, floor, or small illuminated lamp on the left-hand floor. Detection is highly unreliable throughout: frame 1 incorrectly labels the right man’s shoulder and the doorway border as a 'fork'; frame 3 omits both men aside from a minuscule 'person' fragment at the bottom edge representing a foot/garment edge; and frames 4 and 5 combine both overlapping men and their interwoven arms into one continuous 'person' mask.
pose: Throughout the five-frame advance toward the two standing men—from ~1.5–2.0 m away in frame 1 to ~0.3–0.6 m in frame 5—the pose output remains largely empty, identifying only disconnected skeletal pieces when bodies or hands come into view. In frame 1, a yellow body skeleton covers the torso and upper thighs of the left man, who stands ~1.8 m away facing toward and slightly to the camera wearer’s left. Frame 3 adds a magenta hand skeleton on his lowered left hand, ~0.6 m away near his waist and within reach of both the wearer and the two men. Frame 4 contains two magenta hand skeletons that clearly capture the 3D finger articulation and direction of the left man’s raised left palm—~0.3 m before the lens and facing the wearer—and his right hand extending across the right man’s lower arm, ~0.4 m to the right and a little farther back. In frame 5, one magenta skeleton follows the wearer’s own right hand as it touches the left man’s hip from ~0.3 m away. Compared with the blurred movement and heavy shadows in RGB, these hand skeletons reveal the precise finger spread, palm direction, and contact locations far more clearly. Even so, the pose estimator is very unreliable wherever heads and limbs are cropped or self-occluded: it never detects the right-hand man in any frame, misses every body in frames 2–5, and places the yellow head keypoints incorrectly on the left man’s neck/chest in frame 1 because his head lies outside the top of the image.
